title: All four ‘Lord of the Rings’ movie Hobbits explored Boston together this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Sean Astin, Elijah Wood, Dominic Monaghan, and Billy Boyd attended Fan Expo Boston and explored the city together.
They dined at La Royal in Cambridge, a James Beard Award semifinalist, during their stay in Boston.
The group visited local landmarks, including Neptune Oyster and The Green Dragon, an Irish pub in the city.

title: Jaylen Brown to host free Boston block party at Boston Common on Aug. 30
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Jaylen Brown will host '741 Frequency Fest' at Boston Common on August 30 from 2 p.m. to 7 p.m.
The event offers music, games, and giveaways to thank fans after Brown's trade to the Philadelphia 76ers.
The festival is open to the public with no tickets required, highlighting Brown's brand, 741 Frequency.

title: Patriots reportedly releasing 2024 third-round pick Caedan Wallace
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: The Patriots are reportedly releasing offensive guard Caedan Wallace, their 2024 third-round draft pick from Penn State.
Wallace played in 10 games over two seasons, with his offensive snaps decreasing significantly last year.
If Wallace is cut, only Drake Maye and Marcellas Dial Jr. remain from the Patriots' 2024 draft class.

title: Comedian Matt Rife throws down with a paranormal investigator over ‘haunted’ event in Salem
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Comedian Matt Rife faced backlash for telling a paranormal investigator to commit suicide in a now-deleted online comment.
Rife's remark was directed at Chris Mac, who gave an 'online sermon' on the Salem Witch Trials, sparking outrage from his supporters.
The controversy surrounds a Haunted Warren Museum event organized by Rife and Elton Castee, scheduled in Salem on August 27.

title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry, 31, agreed to a two-year extension with the Patriots, potentially worth up to $20 million.
The contract includes $14.5 million in guaranteed money and a $4.2 million signing bonus.
Since joining the Patriots in 2021, Henry has made 259 catches and scored 26 touchdowns.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman crashed a Jaguar into a CVS in Acton, causing significant damage to the store.
Both the driver and her 88-year-old passenger were uninjured, and no CVS shoppers or employees were hurt.
The store at 344 Great Road will remain closed for repairs; the incident is under investigation by Acton Police.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Runway 27 at Boston Logan International Airport will close for about 75 days starting August 31 for safety upgrades.
The project involves installing an Engineered Material Arresting System to prevent runway overruns, impacting flight activity and capacity.
Nearby communities may experience increased air traffic and noise as more flights are rerouted over their areas during construction.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on collision in Sandwich Sunday night left one person dead and three others injured.
The crash occurred near 87 Farmersville Road involving a 2011 Toyota Prius and a 2017 Toyota RAV4.
The Prius driver died after being taken to Cape Cod Hospital; RAV4 occupants suffered nonlife-threatening injuries.

title: Driver on South Shore narrowly escaped before commuter train totaled his Camry
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 33-year-old Mansfield delivery driver exited his stuck Camry before a Commuter Rail train struck it in Cohasset.
The Camry was totaled in the collision with the train on the Greenbush Line; no injuries were reported.
North Main Street was closed for over two hours as authorities investigated and cleared the scene of the crash.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with psychiatrist under cross-examination
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Dr. Jennifer Tufts testified Clancy denied suicidal or homicidal thoughts before killing her children in January 2023.
Clancy's defense argues she was not criminally responsible due to postpartum mental illness influencing her actions.
Clancy's former psychiatrist Tufts mentioned her reluctance to try medications and considered ketamine therapy for severe depression.
